I'm implementing a Roman numeral converter with two functions: `to_roman` and `from_roman`.

For `to_roman`: I use the standard greedy algorithm with a list of (value, symbol) pairs including all subtractive forms (CM, CD, XC, XL, IX, IV). I raise ValueError for inputs outside [1, 3999].

For `from_roman`: I validate that the string is non-empty and contains only valid Roman characters. I then parse the value using the standard right-to-left algorithm (subtracting when a smaller value precedes a larger one). To validate canonicality, I do a round-trip check: if `to_roman(parsed_value) != s`, then `s` is not canonical and I raise ValueError. This elegantly handles all non-canonical forms like IIII, VV, etc.
